sections.overview: This locally recorded moth belongs to the noctuid complex traditionally called Eublemmini and ranges from southern Europe across parts of the eastern Mediterranean to western Asia.
sections.identification: It is a small, patterned moth whose grey-brown forewings bear a contrasting pale central mark; its French name, anthophile écussonnée, refers to its shield-like marking.
sections.habitat: Records come from warm, relatively dry Mediterranean and steppe landscapes, including foothills and open scrub; its scattered observations make local habitat use incompletely known.
sections.diet: Unlike most familiar caterpillars that chew leaves, its larvae are reported to feed on scale insects living on woody plants, including fruit trees.
sections.behavior: Adults are recorded in two seasonal periods in parts of the eastern Mediterranean, with local flight dates varying by region.
sections.reproduction: Published regional accounts report two generations per year in Israel, with adults flying in late spring to early summer and again in late summer; this schedule should not be generalized to every population.
sections.ecology: Calymma is a genus represented by this species in the consulted European catalogues; it is grouped with small Eublemmini moths, but no close same-genus cousin is available for a direct bestiary comparison.
sections.conservation: No global Red List category was found in the consulted sources, and the patchy distribution records do not by themselves justify assigning one.
